anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-level SQL or transaction design that forces the engine to scan, update, or hold more data and longer transactions than business semantics require.
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Concurrent transactions request conflicting locks on the same resources, causing prolonged waits or deadlocks in the lock-manager layer.
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly : Obsolete row versions and undo/rollback records accumulate faster than background cleanup can reclaim them, inflating storage and visibility-check overhead.

When these three root causes coincide, the database experiences an amplified failure mode in which overloaded statements generate large update/delete footprints, each holding locks for extended durations while simultaneously churning out massive version chains. The oversized transactions and wide scans increase lock footprints and hold times, lengthening blocker-waiter chains and raising the probability of deadlocks. Meanwhile, the same long-running or blocked transactions keep old snapshots alive, preventing garbage-collection workers from pruning obsolete versions. The swelling version store enlarges table and index sizes, slows down scans, and drives up buffer churn, which further prolongs statement execution and exacerbates lock hold times. The feedback loop—inefficient SQL inflating work, which intensifies lock contention, which in turn prolongs transactions and stalls cleanup, which then bloats storage and slows access paths—leads to cascading performance degradation, rising latency variance, throughput collapse, and frequent application timeouts or rollbacks.

entry.official_description: Can't initiate database recovery, running in read-only-mode.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
